articles.title: Preso, Peña é transferido para instalação militar, diz jornal | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-presidente paraguaio estava em prisão domiciliar. Movimentação ocorreu horas após ele sofrer impeachment e ter prisão decretada por envolvimento no escândalo do banco ueno, que gerou crise econômica e política no Paraguai.
articles.summary: Ex-presidente paraguaio estava em prisão domiciliar. Movimentação ocorreu horas após ele sofrer impeachment e ter prisão decretada por envolvimento no escândalo do banco ueno, que gerou crise econômica e política no Paraguai.
articles.body:
O ex-presidente do Paraguai Santiago Peña foi transferido para uma instalação militar na madrugada de sexta-feira para sábado (7), horas após sofrer impeachment e ter sua prisão domiciliar decretada.

O ex-presidente foi levado para o Regimiento Escolta Presidencial (REP), uma instalação militar em Assunção utilizada para proteger o presidente paraguaio e sua família, além de autoridades estrangeiras durante visitas oficiais. O REP é como se fosse um quartel de elite das Forças Armadas na capital paraguaia, não uma prisão.

A movimentação ocorreu na noite de sexta, logo antes da meia-noite, segundo o jornal paraguaio "ABC". A transferência de Peña, que está em prisão domiciliar , deu-se por motivos de segurança, porque multidão protestava em frente à sua casa exigindo que ele fosse levado à prisão e houve confronto com a polícia. Sua caravana deixou o local sob xingamentos e ovadas.

Fachada do Regimiento Escolta Presidencial (REP), instalação militar em Assunção, capital do Paraguai, onde o ex-presidente Santiago Peña e sua família foram transferidos em 6 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo

Peña sofreu impeachment e foi destituído da presidência na tarde de sexta-feira, e logo depois ele teve sua prisão decretada por envolvimento no escândalo do banco ueno —que quebrou e causou uma crise econômica e política no Paraguai. O presidente do Banco Central e outras autoridades do país também renunciaram em meio à crise.

O vice de Peña, Pedro Alliana, tomou posse como novo presidente paraguaio já na sexta-feira. Leia aqui quem é Alliana.

O ex-presidente paraguaio é apontado como um dos sócios do grupo controlador do ueno e está sendo investigado por suspeitas de gestão fraudulenta e outros crimes relacionados ao escândalo. Ele comparecerá a uma promotoria federal neste sábado, às 11h no horário de Brasília, no âmbito da investigação contra ele.

Peña negou ter cometido esses crimes. O MP paraguaio ainda deve determinar os fatos específicos e as circunstâncias de cada acusação criminal.

articles.title: EUA oferecem US$ 20 milhões por informações do programa nuclear do Irã | G1
articles.standfirst: Oferta ocorre em meio a rumores de que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, possa ordenar novos bombardeios de grandes proporções contra o programa nuclear iraniano nos próximos dias. Guerra no Oriente Médio já dura oito meses.
articles.summary: Oferta ocorre em meio a rumores de que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, possa ordenar novos bombardeios de grandes proporções contra o programa nuclear iraniano nos próximos dias. Guerra no Oriente Médio já dura oito meses.
articles.body:
Presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e presidente do Irã, Masoud Pezeshkian — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters e Angelina Katsanis/AP Photo

O governo Trump ofereceu na sexta-feira (7) US$ 20 milhões (cerca de R$ 110 milhões) por quem fornecer informações sobre o programa nuclear do Irã .

A oferta, difundida pelo Comando Central do Exército norte-americano, ocorre em meio a rumores de que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump , possa ordenar novos bombardeios de grandes proporções contra o programa nuclear iraniano e após Trump falar que cogita "destruir o resto do Irã" —em referência à guerra no Oriente Médio.

O governo Trump afirmou oferecer "uma recompensa de até US$ 20 milhões e a possibilidade de reassentamento para quem fornecer informações sobre o programa nuclear do Irã, incluindo suas instalações, equipamentos e pessoas envolvidas, como integrantes da comunidade científica, ou sobre o deslocamento de qualquer um desses elementos."

No comunicado, o governo Trump também mencionou um relatório da Agência Internacional de Energia Atômica (AIEA) —órgão da ONU regulador da energia nuclear a nível mundial— que denunciava que o Irã estava enriquecendo urânio acima do nível permitido pelo Tratado de Não Proliferação (TNP) nuclear, do qual o país é signatário. Teerã nega e afirma que seu programa nuclear tem fins pacíficos.

A movimentação ocorre após Trump e outras autoridades do governo dos EUA terem afirmado diversas vezes ao longo dos últimos meses que o programa nuclear iraniano havia sido totalmente destruído —tanto pelo bombardeio surpresa com bombas penetrantes em junho de 2025 quanto na guerra contra o Irã, que já dura oito meses sem previsão de ser finalizada.

Por trás das falas públicas, a Inteligência do governo dos EUA avalia que mesmo após os bombardeios ocorridos durante o conflito, o Irã poderia produzir uma arma nuclear em até um ano. Nos últimos meses, Trump e seu secretário de Guerra, Pete Hegseth, bateram boca por conta da guerra , segundo a imprensa norte-americana.

Trump argumentou que a guerra era necessária para impedir que o Irã desenvolvesse armas nucleares e prometeu que o país do Oriente Médio nunca teria acesso a tal armamento.

Trump culpou a guerra do Irã por derrota histórica nas midterms

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, tira o chapéu por um instante ao sair do espelho d'água do Lincoln Memorial, após sua reabertura depois de meses de reformas, em Washington, DC, EUA, em 2 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Umit Bektas TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY

Nesta semana, Trump reconheceu afirmado que a guerra contra o Irã contribuiu para a d errota do Partido Republicano nas eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA , conhecidas como midterms.

👉O partido do presidente perdeu a maioria na Câmara e no Senado, em um movimento chamado pela imprensa americana de "onda azul", em referência à cor do Partido Democrata.

Na ocasião, Trump foi questionado se o ataque valeu a pena. Ele respondeu que sim: "Bem, não há escolha... Tem que ser feito. Não se pode deixar o Irã ter uma arma nuclear, ou tudo o que vocês veem aqui pode, um dia, deixar de existir."

A guerra contra o Irã, iniciada por EUA e Israel em 28 de fevereiro, provocou uma disparada nos preços dos combustíveis, nas passagens aéreas e na inflação geral. Estimativas apontam que a guerra custou o equivalente a até US$ 100 bilhões (cerca de R$ 508 bilhões) aos cofres americanos, segundo fontes do Pentágono.

articles.title: Praia Grande mapeia população negra para plano de igualdade racial | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento fica disponível até 30 de novembro e será usado na elaboração de políticas públicas de saúde, educação e cultura.
articles.summary: Levantamento fica disponível até 30 de novembro e será usado na elaboração de políticas públicas de saúde, educação e cultura.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Praia Grande realiza mapeamento da população negra na cidade. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Praia Grande

Praia Grande , no litoral de São Paulo, iniciou um mapeamento da população negra da cidade para auxiliar na elaboração do Plano Municipal de Políticas Públicas de Promoção da Igualdade Racial. Os moradores podem participar do levantamento até 30 de novembro.

A iniciativa ocorre no mês da Consciência Negra, celebrada em 20 de novembro. Segundo a prefeitura, as informações coletadas serão usadas no planejamento de políticas públicas nas áreas de saúde, educação e cultura, além de auxiliar no cumprimento da legislação federal sobre igualdade racial.

O levantamento é feito por meio de um formulário digital disponibilizado pela Secretaria de Diversidade e Inclusão (Sedi). Os moradores podem participar até 30 de novembro.

Segundo a prefeitura, o objetivo é reunir informações mais precisas sobre as características e necessidades da população negra do município para orientar a criação de políticas públicas.

Ivanilda Josefa da Silva, representante da Divisão de Igualdade Social da Sedi, afirmou que Praia Grande ainda enfrenta dificuldades na coleta de dados estatísticos relacionados à identificação de raça e cor.

Segundo ela, a falta dessas informações dificulta a implementação de políticas públicas já previstas em âmbito nacional, como a Política Nacional de Saúde Integral da População Negra, que estabelece diretrizes para melhorar o atendimento e prevê a criação de comitês específicos.

A elaboração do plano municipal busca, de acordo com a prefeitura, alinhar as ações de Praia Grande às políticas nacionais de promoção da igualdade racial.

A expectativa da administração municipal é que o mapeamento ajude a estabelecer instrumentos técnicos e jurídicos para garantir direitos, combater desigualdades e desenvolver ações permanentes de promoção da igualdade racial na cidade.

articles.title: Navio Buenavista suspende saídas no Brasil após reclamações | G1
articles.standfirst: Corazul Buenavista estreou no Brasil na última semana e foi alvo de reclamações sobre piscinas vazias, filas nos restaurantes e chuveiros com água gelada. Companhia suspendeu quatro saídas para implementar melhorias e solucionar problemas técnicos e operacionais.
articles.summary: A Corazul Cruceros suspendeu as saídas do navio Buenavista para corrigir falhas técnicas e operacionais após queixas de passageiros sobre a estrutura na estreia.
articles.body:
A Corazul Cruceros suspendeu as saídas do navio Buenavista previstas para a temporada de cruzeiros até a próxima sexta-feira (13). Atracada no Porto de Santos (SP) , a embarcação foi alvo de uma série de reclamações dos hóspedes. Segundo a empresa, o período será utilizado para implementar melhorias e solucionar pendências técnicas.

O navio, que estreou no Brasil, deu início à temporada de cruzeiros 2026/2027 na última sexta-feira (30). Durante a viagem inaugural, no entanto, hóspedes relataram problemas como piscinas vazias, filas nos restaurantes e chuveiros com água gelada. Diante das reclamações, a Corazul e a R11 Travel, distribuidora oficial da armadora no Brasil, anunciaram medidas de compensação aos passageiros.

Inicialmente, a R11 informou que os problemas haviam sido resolvidos para os embarques seguintes. Porém, nesta sexta-feira (6), a companhia anunciou a suspensão de quatro saídas previstas em Santos (SP) e no Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

De acordo com o comunicado, a decisão foi tomada para avaliar os comentários e as percepções dos passageiros, identificar oportunidades de melhoria e resolver questões técnicas e operacionais que exigem atenção adicional.

O navio Buenavista, da empresa espanhola Corazul, chegou ao Porto de Santos — Foto: Sílvio Luiz/A Tribuna Jornal

A Corazul destacou que a medida considera a proximidade da alta temporada de cruzeiros. “Em vez de realizar essas atividades durante as viagens regulares, a empresa entende que é do interesse de seus hóspedes concluir o trabalho necessário enquanto a embarcação permanece atracada no porto”, informou.

Uma das saídas estava prevista para esta sexta-feira (6). Segundo a Corazul, os hóspedes que desejarem embarcar poderão aproveitar a experiência a bordo, incluindo as instalações, a gastronomia e o entretenimento do navio, até segunda-feira (9).

“Todos os hóspedes afetados por esses ajustes receberão o reembolso integral do valor pago”, ressaltou a companhia.

A Corazul disse que agradece sinceramente a compreensão, a paciência e o apoio de seus hóspedes e parceiros de viagem enquanto a empresa dá esses importantes passos rumo a uma temporada inaugural de sucesso no Brasil.

O navio Buenavista, da empresa espanhola Corazul, chegou ao Porto de Santos — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/A Tribuna Jornal

A primeira viagem do Buenavista no Brasil começou na sexta-feira (30), no Porto de Santos, com escalas no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e em Búzios (RJ). O navio retornou ao Terminal de Passageiros Giusfredo Santini na segunda-feira (2).

Ao atracar no Porto de Santos para o início do cruzeiro, as manchas de ferrugem no casco do navio chamaram atenção, mas os problemas começaram após o início do embarque, que teve atrasos significativos. Veja a lista do que os passageiros relataram abaixo:

➡️Piscinas vazias e jacuzzi sem funcionar;

➡️Tempo de escala em Búzios foi reduzido;

➡️Cassino ainda não estava instalado no navio;

➡️Falta de água potável na noite de 30 de outubro;

➡️Confusão e filas nos serviços de bares e restaurantes;

➡️Aparelhos de ar-condicionado com problemas de funcionamento;

➡️Algumas cabines não abriram com os cartões magnéticos porque a bateria da fechadura eletrônica havia descarregado.

A maioria dos problemas foi sendo resolvida ao longo do cruzeiro, ainda de acordo com os relatos dos hóspedes.

O cruzeiro, de bandeira das Bermudas, tem 260 metros de comprimento, 13 conveses e capacidade para 2.140 passageiros. A estrutura reúne opções de gastronomia, lazer, compras e bem-estar, além de espaços dedicados a crianças e adolescentes, como:

Entre as opções de alimentação estão dois restaurantes principais, buffet, churrascaria e espaço para lanches. O navio também dispõe de bares de coquetéis, esportes e piscina, além de um café.

A estrutura de lazer e entretenimento inclui cassino, teatro, cinema, discoteca, biblioteca, academia, hidromassagens e spa. Há ainda lojas e espaços dedicados a crianças e adolescentes.

Para o público infantil, o navio oferece o clube Jovem Tripulação, dividido por faixas etárias de 3 a 5, de 6 a 9 e de 10 a 12 anos. Já o Buenaonda Club é destinado a adolescentes a partir de 13 anos.

articles.title: Paraná registra estragos, quedas de árvores e falta de luz | G1
articles.standfirst: Paraná está sob alerta de tempestades do Inmet.
articles.summary: Paraná está sob alerta de tempestades do Inmet.
articles.body:
Diversas cidades do Paraná registraram estragos, quedas de árvores e falta de luz durante chuvas intensas no começo da tarde deste sábado (7).

Em Curitiba , uma árvore de grande porte caiu no Pilarzinho e bloqueia a Avenida Fredolin Wolf. Um carro não viu e bateu, sem gravidade.

Árvore de grande porte caiu no Pilarzinho — Foto: Douglas Santucci/RPC

Quedas de árvores também foram registradas no Capão Raso, Santa Felicidade, São Braz, Hauer e Boqueirão.

Cidades da Região Metropolitana da capital paranaense também registraram estragos, entre elas, Pinhais , São José dos Pinhais e Araucária .

Araucária de grande porte caiu em Pinhais — Foto: Edilson Silva

Além da queda de uma araucária de grande porte em Pinhais, um condomínio da cidade registrou o desabamento da estrutura do estacionamento. Apesar dos danos materiais, ninguém se feriu.

Dados da Copel indicam ao menos 275 mil imóveis sem energia elétrica no Paraná no começo da tarde deste sábado. Sendo 107.358 imóveis em Curitiba, 18.316 imóveis em São José dos Pinhais e 10.476 em Itaperuçu .

O Paraná está sob alerta de tempestades do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet). Segundo a Climatempo, os temporais devem ser mais intensos nas cidades do sul e do sudoeste, mas em algumas partes do norte do estado os ventos também podem chegar a 90 km/h.

Pavilhão de igreja desabou em Laranjeiras do Sul

Pavilhão de igreja desabou em Laranjeiras do Sul — Foto: Janice Aparecida Couto Nessa

As paredes do pavilhão da igreja Comunidade São Francisco de Assis desabaram em Laranjeiras do Sul.

Metade do telhado do espaço já havia sido arrancado pelo temporal que atingiu a cidade em 4 de outubro deste ano, quando a rajada do vento atingiu 124 quilômetros por hora, danificando 850 residências.

Neste sábado, a chuva forte atingiu novamente a cidade, com ventos de até 80 quilômetros por hora, por volta das 11h da manhã, segundo o Simepar. Com isso, as paredes do espaço caíram.

O pavilhão estava desocupado e não era utilizado desde o temporal do início de outubro. De acordo com a ministra da igreja, Janice Aparecida Couto Nessa, apenas banheiros e a cozinha do espaço ficaram em pé.

"É triste isso, muito triste, porque esse pavilhão tem uma história linda, é um dos mais antigos aqui das comunidades. A nossa comunidade é uma das mais antigas e o pavilhão também. Muita história, casamento, festas, teatros, parte esportiva, recreativa, a catequese, a gente fazia ali, tinha o uso, e agora aconteceu isso", lamentou.

Apesar da chuva forte e vento sobre Laranjeiras do Sul, bombeiros não registraram ocorrências relacionadas a temporal na cidade.

Ao menos 17 cidades registraram rajadas de vento acima de 50 km/h neste sábado, até as 13h15, nas estações meteorológicas do Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar):

Distrito de Entre Rios, em Guarapuava: 56,2 km/h às 11h30

Distrito de Horizonte, em Palmas: 70,9 km/h às 9h15

Santa Maria do Oeste: 90,7 km/h às 12h15

articles.title: Chuvas em Santa Catarina: Cidades em emergência sofrem novos temporais | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Defesa Civil, enxurradas e alagamentos foram registrados em Abdon Batista, Vargem e Zortéa, municípios que já tinham decretado situação de emergência ao longo da semana.
articles.summary: Chuvas em Santa Catarina provocam enxurradas e alagamentos em Abdon Batista, Vargem e Zortéa, cidades que já estavam em situação de emergência após tornados.
articles.body:
Chuvas intensas voltaram a causar estragos no Oeste de Santa Catarina na manhã deste sábado (7). Ao longo da semana, três tornados - sendo dois na região - e duas microexplosões foram confirmados no estado pela Defesa Civil.

Segundo o órgão estadual, enxurradas e alagamentos foram registrados em Abdon Batista, Vargem e Zortéa nas primeiras horas do dia. As três cidades estão entre as 62 que já tinham decretado situação de emergência ao longo da semana . Em Rio do Sul , no Vale do Itajaí, um muro de contenção da BR-470 caiu sobre veículos (assista acima).

Desde domingo (1º), o estado registra estragos causados por tempestades. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, 126 municípios haviam confirmado danos, e pelo menos 6.413 residências tinham sido atingidas.

Em Abdon Batista, a enxurrada inundou o Centro, danificou dois prédios públicos e atingiu várias casas.

O município registrou 184 milímetros de chuva em apenas 12 horas, entre a noite de sexta-feira (6) e a manhã de sábado. Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais da prefeitura, o prefeito Lucimar Salmória pediu que os moradores procurem locais seguros.

“Abdon amanheceu literalmente embaixo d’água. Pedimos à toda a população cautela, e que vão para um lugar seguro. Nossas equipes estão se mobilizando para fazer tudo que estiver a seu alcance para o mais brevemente possível darmos uma resposta a todos”, afirmou.

Temporais causam estragos em Abdon Batista — Foto: Reprodução

Vargem também registrou alagamentos na área central. Um prédio público e outras casas foram danificados. Em Zortéa, o temporal alagou o Centro e atingiu dezenas de moradias.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, a Defesa Civil não havia contabilizado o número total de imóveis atingidos nos municípios neste sábado.

➡️ O cenário preocupa também em outras regiões. Em Rio do Sul, o acumulado de chuva superou em mais que o dobro o volume inicialmente previsto para todo o fim de semana.

No bairro Canoas, um muro de contenção da BR-470 cedeu e atingiu diversos carros (foto abaixo) . Segundo a prefeitura, ninguém ficou ferido.

muro de contenção da Br-470 em Rio do Sul cedeu neste sábado — Foto: Jari Silva/Arquivo pessoal

Barragem em Rio do Sul (SC) — Foto: Reprodução

➡️ Em Blumenau , no Vale do Itajaí, a Estação de Tratamento de Água (ETA) 1 teve o tratamento de água totalmente paralisado na manhã deste sábado após um deslizamento de terra provocar a queda de um poste, que afetou o abastecimento de energia no local.

Defesa Civil e Celesc foram acionadas para avaliar a situação. Não há previsão para a retomada das atividades da estação, que é responsável por abastecer cinco bairros da região central: Boa Vista, Victor Konder, Centro, Ponta Aguda e Nova Esperança.

articles.title: The Lions by the River Tigris: Restoring Mosul’s artefacts
articles.summary: When the ancient Iraqi city of Mosul is devastated after liberation from ISIL, three men strive to revive its beauty.
articles.body:
In the heart of war-ravaged Mosul, two carved lions stand as a fragile link to the city’s shattered past. Bashar, a fisherman, lost his once-grand family home during the battle to liberate the city from ISIL (ISIS) nearly 10 years ago. All that remains is a marble gate crowned with lions, which he fiercely guards.

Fakhri, a devoted collector determined to save Mosul’s heritage, becomes obsessed with acquiring the lions gate for his unofficial museum. His friend Fadil, a musician once silenced under ISIL, challenges him to see the human cost behind every artefact. As Mosul rebuilds, a quiet cultural revival reflects the resilience of a city with 8,000 years of history.

The Lions by the River Tigris is a documentary film by Zaradasht Ahmed.

articles.title: Enem: estudantes terão metrô, trem e ônibus de graça em SP nos dias de prova | G1
articles.standfirst: Gratuidade no transporte metropolitano vale para os dias 8 e 15 de novembro. Governo também vai disponibilizar cerca de 7 mil ônibus para alunos da rede estadual em mais de 500 cidades.
articles.summary: Gratuidade no transporte metropolitano vale para os dias 8 e 15 de novembro. Governo também vai disponibilizar cerca de 7 mil ônibus para alunos da rede estadual em mais de 500 cidades.
articles.body:
Movimento na estação Sé, da linha 3-Vermelha. — Foto: Letícia Dauer/g1

Todos os estudantes que vão fazer o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) terão transporte público metropolitano gratuito no estado de São Paulo neste domingo (8) e no próximo (15), dias de aplicação das provas. A medida vale das 9h às 21h e não exige a apresentação de comprovante de escolaridade.

A gratuidade contempla as linhas da Companhia Paulista de Trens Metropolitanos (CPTM), do Metrô e das concessionárias Motiva, TIC Trens e Trivia Trens, além dos ônibus intermunicipais e do Veículo Leve sobre Trilhos (VLT).

Segundo o governo estadual, o benefício será válido em todas as regiões metropolitanas de São Paulo.

Para atender os candidatos, as empresas de transporte terão trens reservas disponíveis em todas as linhas, que poderão ser colocados em circulação caso haja aumento da demanda. Também haverá reforço nas equipes de atendimento nas estações.

Transporte gratuito para alunos da rede estadual

O governo estadual também vai disponibilizar aproximadamente 7 mil ônibus para transportar cerca de 70 mil estudantes da rede estadual de ensino até os locais de prova, em mais de 500 municípios.

A operação, coordenada pela Secretaria da Educação (Seduc-SP), é realizada pela primeira vez e atende estudantes que vivem em cidades sem previsão de gratuidade no transporte coletivo durante o Enem ou que não têm acesso a linhas que atendam seus locais de residência ou de prova.

Os ônibus poderão buscar os alunos em casa ou em pontos de encontro previamente definidos. Para estudantes com deficiência, o atendimento será feito de porta a porta.

O transporte será organizado pelas 91 Unidades Regionais de Ensino (UREs), conforme a necessidade de cada município. Os estudantes e seus familiares devem procurar a unidade responsável pela escola para consultar os locais de embarque e as orientações para os dias de prova.

Segundo a Seduc-SP, 315,2 mil alunos da 3ª série do Ensino Médio da rede estadual estão inscritos no Enem neste ano, o equivalente a 94,3% dos matriculados.

articles.standfirst: Ex-presidente paraguaio depõe após prisão decretada por envolvimento no escândalo do banco ueno, que gerou crise econômica e política no Paraguai.
articles.summary: Ex-presidente paraguaio depõe após prisão decretada por envolvimento no escândalo do banco ueno, que gerou crise econômica e política no Paraguai.
articles.body:
O ex-presidente do Paraguai , Santiago Peña , chegou à Procuradoria-Geral neste sábado (7) para prestar depoimento aos promotores, um dia após sofrer um processo de impeachment e ser colocado em prisão domiciliar. Ele é investigado pelos supostos crimes de quebra de confiança, tráfico de influências e administração em lucros próprios.

Segundo a AFP, o procurador Christian Benítez, encarregado da investigação, disse à imprensa local que serão apresentados fatos e provas, e que "no decorrer da tarde" poderá ser formalmente acusado . Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia informação do que foi dito no depoimento.

O depoimento acontece em meio a uma crise política e financeira desencadeada pelo colapso da instituição financeira digital ueno. Os promotores informaram, na sexta-feira, que as acusações contra Peña ainda estavam sendo definidas, mas poderiam incluir tráfico de influência.

Ex-presidente foi transferido para instalação militar

O ex-presidente do Paraguai Santiago Peña foi transferido para uma instalação militar na madrugada de sexta-feira para sábado (7), horas após sofrer impeachment e ter sua prisão domiciliar decretada.

O ex-presidente foi levado para o Regimiento Escolta Presidencial (REP), uma instalação militar em Assunção utilizada para proteger o presidente paraguaio e sua família, além de autoridades estrangeiras durante visitas oficiais. O REP é como se fosse um quartel de elite das Forças Armadas na capital paraguaia, não uma prisão.

A movimentação ocorreu na noite de sexta, logo antes da meia-noite, segundo o jornal paraguaio "ABC". A transferência de Peña, que está em prisão domiciliar , deu-se por motivos de segurança, porque uma multidão protestava em frente à sua casa exigindo que ele fosse levado à prisão e houve confronto com a polícia. Sua caravana deixou o local sob xingamentos e ovadas.

Fachada do Regimiento Escolta Presidencial (REP), instalação militar em Assunção, capital do Paraguai, onde o ex-presidente Santiago Peña e sua família foram transferidos em 6 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo

Peña sofreu impeachment e foi destituído da presidência na tarde de sexta-feira, e logo depois ele teve sua prisão decretada por envolvimento no escândalo do banco ueno —que quebrou e causou uma crise econômica e política no Paraguai. O presidente do Banco Central e outras autoridades do país também renunciaram em meio à crise.

O vice de Peña, Pedro Alliana, tomou posse como novo presidente paraguaio já na sexta-feira. Leia aqui quem é Alliana.

O ex-presidente paraguaio é apontado como um dos sócios do grupo controlador do ueno e está sendo investigado por suspeitas de gestão fraudulenta e outros crimes relacionados ao escândalo. Ele comparecerá a uma promotoria federal neste sábado, às 11h no horário de Brasília, no âmbito da investigação contra ele.

articles.title: Hemsby beach homes face demolition months after being sold
articles.summary: One property investor from Manchester bought a home six weeks ago, now it is deemed unsafe.
articles.body:
A property investor and a woman planning for her retirement have been told their homes are at risk of falling into the sea just months after they purchased them.

The two properties are part of a collection of former fishermen's cottages in the hamlet of Newport, south of Hemsby, Norfolk.

The houses, which were both bought in the last three months, are among nine properties in the area deemed to be at risk of coastal erosion.

Great Yarmouth Borough Council has advised the homeowners to leave their properties for their own safety.

Nathan Weissbraun, who lives in Manchester, paid £60,000 in September for his three-bed house in Newport, which is part of a row of four terraced cottages.

Weissbraun, who owns about 20 rental properties, said he paid £55,000 less than the previous owner did when they bought the house in 2023.

"It was below market value, so it was a good price. It's a lot of money we're going to lose and we're trying to fight our corner so it can stay," he added.

He said the house was the "first and last" property he would consider buying in Norfolk - a county he said he had never visited.

Lynn Sweet, 64, bought a four-bed cottage and two-bed annexe in Newport in August at auction for £145,000.

She said it seemed an "ideal opportunity" and hoped she could rent out the larger cottage to support herself during her retirement.

Eight weeks later, she was told the home was unsafe and would need to be demolished.

Sweet said she was aware of the erosion dangers in Hemsby, but thought she would have at least 10 to 20 years there.

Auction House East Anglia said it recognised the distress being experienced by homeowners in Hemsby, but said vendors were entitled to sell their properties.

Bryan Baxter, the firm's director, said: "We endeavour to ensure that relevant information about a property's condition, location and known risks is disclosed to prospective purchasers.

"Where coastal erosion is a factor, we make buyers aware that they should carry out their own research into any issues likely to affect the property or land."

Gemma Lomas, who is the fourth generation of her family to have lived in the Newport cottages, said learning the homes were at risk and now unsafe "came as a shock".

"In 2015, we were told we would have 100 years, last year this fell to 30 years, now we are being told it could be weeks.

"These homes have stood here for 200 years, they are an important part of Newport's maritime history," she said.

The homeowners have called for the council to provide more evidence the homes were unsafe, left the speed of the demolition process would not give them time to gain answers.

The council said it was acting responsibly to ensure the safety of the public.

A spokesperson for the authority said: "Where property is at risk of collapse on to the beach, demolition needs to be carried out in a safe and manageable way.

"Analysis of the latest data and mapping shows nine properties are now within the 10m zone of risk and owners have been contacted and spoken with to encourage them to vacate in a timely way so any necessary action can be taken in a safe and planned way."

Last winter, the dunes in Hemsby saw about 50% of the erosion predicted for the next 30 years, the council said, with more than 10m of land lost in over 12 months.

Since December 2025, 41 properties have also been demolished.

There is currently no compensation scheme for people who have lost homes to erosion, but there is a trial scheme that offers homeowners the ability to relocate.

Last year the Environment Agency gave £1.6m to Great Yarmouth Borough Council to enable the authority to buy planning rights from owners of properties at immediate risk of coastal erosion, which provided them with the financial means and legal planning permission to relocate.

James Bensly, a Great Yarmouth First councillor who represents East Flegg on the authority, said he "finds it very uncomfortable" to see properties advertised for sale when the "risk of them falling into the sea is so high".

"However, I also appreciate the sellers' point of view, and ultimately you cannot stop someone from putting a property on the market or another person from choosing to buy it," he added.

He urged prospective buyers to do research before purchasing a property to ensure they are aware of any risks.

articles.title: US Senator Abdul El-Sayed launches ‘Habibi’ political action committee
articles.summary: The first Muslim senator’s new committee will let him raise money for other candidates.
articles.body:
Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has launched a political action committee called “Habibi PAC”, days after becoming the first Muslim member of the United States Senate.

Political action committees, or PACs, are organisations that raise and spend money to support or oppose candidates for office.

A Federal Election Commission filing dated on Thursday shows that Habibi PAC is registered as a leadership PAC sponsored by El-Sayed. Such committees are separate from a politician’s own campaign.

Habibi, an Arabic term of endearment meaning “my dear” or “my beloved”, is a word El-Sayed used often on the campaign trail, including in his victory speech in Detroit, when he addressed Vice President JD Vance directly: “JD, habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January.”

He is one of several newly elected Democrats to register leadership PACs since Tuesday’s vote, according to FEC filings. They include Arizona Congressman-elect Amish Shah’s “PACStreet Boy”, Iowa Senator-elect Josh Turek’s “WheelPAC” and North Carolina Senator-elect Roy Cooper’s “One NC PAC”.

According to OpenSecrets, ambitious lawmakers use leadership PACs to gain clout with colleagues and strengthen bids for leadership posts or committee chairmanships by giving to other members, their party and other political committees.

In the 2024 election cycle, leadership PACs gave $79.3m to federal candidates. Most went to Republicans, although a Democratic leadership PAC was the biggest single donor.

El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, defeated Republican Mike Rogers after a campaign in which Trump, Vance and Senator Ted Cruz questioned his loyalty, called him a “jihadist” and attempted to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood movement, without providing any evidence.

Speaking to Al Jazeera at a rally in the Michigan city of Wyandotte days before the vote, El-Sayed said taxpayers’ money should be spent saving lives at home rather than going to foreign governments committing genocide or apartheid.

He added that defeating Trump was not enough and that the system that produced him had to be replaced.

Getting money out of politics was one of his central pledges. In his victory speech, he said the result showed that in a battle between money and the many, “the many can win”.

His win came amid the most expensive midterm election on record. According to an analysis of FEC data by OpenSecrets, total spending is expected to reach $11.9bn, up from $8.9bn in 2022.

Outside spending, driven by super PACs, is projected to hit $3.9bn, an 85 percent increase on 2022. So-called dark money from undisclosed donors has already reached at least $1.47bn, surpassing the 2024 record of $1.35bn, which included the presidential race.

OpenSecrets found that conservative groups outspent liberal ones on outside spending by about $360m, while Democratic candidates were expected to outspend Republican candidates by roughly $800m.

articles.title: '36 missiles, 172 drones': Russia to join US-Ukraine talks after massive overnight strikes on Kyiv energy sites
articles.summary: Russia launched 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones at Ukraine overnight, targeting energy infrastructure in Kyiv and surrounding regions, even as Moscow
articles.body: Russia launched 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones at Ukraine overnight, targeting energy infrastructure in Kyiv and surrounding regions, even as Moscow prepares to join trilateral talks with the United States and Ukraine next week.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said all 36 missiles were directed at Kyiv and the surrounding region, with energy facilities bearing the brunt of the attacks. The strikes also damaged residential buildings, the Northern Bridge and a kindergarten, while disrupting electricity, water and heating supplies in the capital.A substation connecting the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine was hit in the Kyiv region. Other substations were damaged in Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipro. Twelve regions, apart from Kyiv, came under attack, leaving nine people injured, including a child, Zelenskyy said."Russia is preparing for trilateral talks by launching ballistic missiles at Ukraine’s critical infrastructure," Zelenskyy said, adding that repair and rescue operations were underway wherever the security situation allowed. He also called on the United States to increase bilateral support and maintain Ukraine among its policy priorities.Meanwhile, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Interfax that Russia's delegation for the talks with the US and Ukraine would include senior military officials and diplomats.The meeting is scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday and will be the first trilateral engagement of its kind since February.The Russian delegation will again be led by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky and include deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov, who will join the negotiations for the first time, along with senior General Staff officer Yuri Zhigarlovsky.Deputy foreign minister Mikhail Galuzin and military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov are also expected to participate.Russian President Vladimir Putin met the delegation at a security council meeting on Friday to discuss preparations for the talks. articles.title: Johnny Marr guitar could fetch £30k at Wiltshire auction
articles.summary: The Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The.
articles.body:
A guitar used by Johnny Marr after his split from The Smiths could fetch up to £30,000 when it goes under the hammer next month.

The white Fender American Vintage 1962 Reissue Stratocaster was played during Marr's time with British rock band The The which he joined in 1988, a year after leaving The Smiths.

Auctioneers Gardiner Houlgate said a private owner bought the guitar in 2020, with Marr - originally from Manchester - signing the guitar's headstock at the time and providing a handwritten postcard describing how it had been used.

The guitar will go on sale at the Gardiner Houlgate auction house in Corsham, Wiltshire, on 8 December where it is estimated to fetch between £20,000 and £30,000.

Luke Hobbs, auctioneer at Gardiner Houlgate, said: "We're valuing this guitar at around £20,000 to £30,000 based on other recent sales of Johnny Marr's instruments.

"Marr's equipment is very popular with collectors and fans.

"Now in his 60s, he's become something of a national treasure in the UK."

Other guitars owned by Marr fetched almost £4m at an auction at Christie's in London in September.

Marr joined The The following a brief period with The Pretenders.

He used the white Fender Stratocaster on stage during The The Versus The World tour which took place in 1989 and 1990.

The guitar can be seen in a film of the tour, also called The The Versus The World.

Recently, Marr has written and recorded with Gorillaz, Billie Eilish, Franz Ferdinand and Noel Gallagher's High Flying Birds.

The guitar will be available for public viewing at Gardiner Houlgate ahead of the auction. It can be seen by members of the public on 4, 7 and 8 December.

articles.summary: Iran on Saturday claimed significant military gains during its conflict with the United States, asserting that it downed hundreds of hostile aircraft and
articles.body: Iran on Saturday claimed significant military gains during its conflict with the United States, asserting that it downed hundreds of hostile aircraft and strengthened its domestic defence manufacturing capabilities, through underground “missile production cities”Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi claimed the country downed 260 hostile aircraft during the US-Iran conflict. These included F-35, F-16, F-5 and F-18 fighter jets, as well as MQ-1, RQ-4, Orbiter and Lucas drones, Mehr News Agency reported.Additionally, the official said Tehran had intercepted seven reconnaissance aircraft over the past two weeks.“We have brought down seven MQM-170 reconnaissance drones intact. This is nothing but a demonstration of our technological superiority over the enemy,” Mohebbi said.The spokesperson claimed Iran’s defence force has rapidly transferred its missile and drone production lines from the surface to underground facilities, moving beyond underground missile storage complexes to establish “missile production cities” deep beneath the ground, utilising domestic technical capabilities and geographical advantages.According to local media, Iran has rapidly developed its national defence networks following months of intense military hostility with the United States and its Gulf allies, and now possesses advanced capabilities.“If another war breaks out, the world will witness the IRGC Aerospace Force’s new capabilities, and our enemies will be astonished by its strength and power,” Mohebbi claimed.Iran also claimed it was exporting defence equipment like Arman missiles, the 358 loitering munition and the Khordad-3 air defence system, while also meeting domestic demands.“Today, in addition to meeting domestic needs, we have become an exporter of defence equipment and products—a significant achievement for the country.”The United States and Israel carried out extensive strikes on Iranian nuclear and military installations during 2025 and 2026, saying their operations were aimed at preventing Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons and deterring its nuclear ambitions.US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has played down the confrontation, insisting that it should not be described as a war. He claimed Washington had made substantial progress in dealing with Iran and was extracting more oil than it had before the hostilities."We made a lot of progress with Iran. We’re taking out more oil now than we were before the war. It’s not a war. It can’t be a war when for five months nobody was hurt, killed, or anything else. It’s not a war," Trump said.His remarks came after the Republican Party suffered setbacks in the US midterm elections, prompting a softer tone from the US President.The war with Iran emerged as one of the factors behind the Republican Party's poor performance in the midterm elections, with the conflict adding to public dissatisfaction over rising fuel prices and the cost of living. The prolonged military campaign and its economic consequences became a liability for Trump and Republican candidates, particularly among voters who wanted the administration to focus on domestic concerns rather than a foreign conflict.Vice President JD Vance attributed the party's defeat to the war, writing on social media, "The reason we lost is the war."Trump acknowledged that the conflict had hurt Republicans electorally, although he defended the decision to launch military action against Iran.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sudan war and climate change see parents struggle to feed their children
articles.summary: War, poverty and climate change are all affecting Sudanese, with increasing cases of child malnutrition.
articles.body:
Port Sudan, Sudan – After a two-and-a-half-hour journey from the village of al-Lalouba, Layla Ali arrived in Port Sudan to get help for her five-year-old son, Adam. His severe malnutrition had left his ribs visibly protruding beneath his skin.

He had begun to lose his appetite two weeks earlier and became too sick to move. The distance to the hospital and Ali’s fears about the cost of treatment stopped her from rushing Adam for medical treatment. But when his condition deteriorated further, Ali had no choice but to rush him to hospital.

“We spent five days in hospital while my son received treatment. He suffers from recurring bouts of malnutrition, but this time we brought him to hospital because I was afraid he might die,” Ali told Al Jazeera.

“When Adam became ill, he would stop eating. I used to give him the usual meals we prepared at home, mostly porridge and milk. But the doctors have now helped me understand which foods are appropriate for his age and the nutrients he needs.”

Adam’s condition reflects a wider crisis facing children across Sudan, where a civil war has continued since April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary.

The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) estimates that 825,000 children under five will suffer from severe acute malnutrition in 2026, a 7 percent increase from 2025.

In the first six months of this year, UNICEF and its partners treated 174,700 children with severe acute malnutrition nationwide. The Port Sudan Teaching Hospital has recorded 433 cases between January and August this year.

Maryam Gadalsid, a nutrition counsellor at the hospital, said the number of children admitted with malnutrition continues to rise, forcing medical staff to accommodate as many as possible.

But this has led to overcrowding, with three children to a single bed in the hospital’s 17-bed malnutrition unit, Gadalsid told Al Jazeera, increasing the risk of disease spreading among patients.

“Medical staff assess each child’s condition before providing essential supplies, including therapeutic milk and other nutritional supplies free of charge, with support from the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF,” Gadalsid said. “However, intravenous fluids and medication remain a significant financial burden for many families, struggling with the economic crisis caused by the war.”

Gadalsid added that inadequate nutrition among pregnant women, driven by displacement and economic hardship, was also putting their babies at risk of poor growth and malnutrition.

An increase in the numbers of flies, which can contaminate food and water, and mosquitoes, which transmit malaria, was worrying, she said. Malnourished children, in particular, are at risk of these diseases and viruses.

“With the onset of winter, malnutrition cases increase [and] … the number of flies rises, contributing to the spread of diseases that cause malnutrition,” she said.

Displaced children face worsening malnutrition

The situation is particularly bad in western Sudan’s Darfur region, which had already faced two decades of war before the 2023 nationwide conflict broke out.

Darfur has been an epicentre of the current conflict and is currently an RSF stronghold. Fighting there, combined with hunger and disease, has created an increasingly desperate situation for millions of civilians, particularly women and children.

In North Darfur alone, there were at least 40,000 cases of malnutrition between January and May 2025, according to UNICEF, when the RSF imposed a siege on the state’s capital, el-Fasher. The city was later taken by the RSF in October, and the paramilitary group is accused of killing thousands of civilians there.

Meanwhile, in Blue Nile State, southeastern Sudan, malnutrition is also taking a growing toll on displaced children.

Sabri Adam, deputy head of the committee overseeing al-Karama 3 displacement camp, which is located in the state capital al-Damazin, told Al Jazeera that cases of malnutrition had risen from 1,800 in September to 2,116 in November, accounting for more than a quarter of the camp’s children. Of those affected, 1,760 are under the age of five.

According to Adam, al-Karama 3 is home to more than 7,600 children under the age of 10, among almost 4,000 displaced families. They had fled areas in western Blue Nile State, including al-Tadamon, Bau and Kurmuk, where military operations between the SAF and the RSF have intensified.

“These families arrived at the camp in extremely difficult humanitarian conditions, amid limited funding and humanitarian assistance from organisations, and a lack of health monitoring despite the growing needs of displaced people,” he said to Al Jazeera.

Adam said the camp received cash assistance from the Red Crescent earlier this month to support people affected by malnutrition and pregnant women. Each eligible household received 620,000 Sudanese pounds (about $60 at the parallel market rate).

The situation is unfolding as the IPC warns of a growing risk of famine across parts of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan. Conflict, mass displacement, severe drought and inadequate humanitarian funding are driving a further deterioration in food security.

The El Nino climate phenomenon has led to reduced rainfall in Sudan during the rainy season, leading to drought that is affecting roughly half of the country.

According to the IPC, nearly two-thirds of farmland in North Darfur and roughly half in South Darfur and Kordofan states have had poor vegetation growth, threatening harvests and leaving families facing higher prices and worsening hunger.

War and poverty deepen Sudan’s malnutrition crisis

Back at the Port Sudan Teaching Hospital, Dr Ahmed Youssef, the medical director of the paediatric department, said increasing malnutrition was driven not only by the effects of war and displacement but also by limited nutrition awareness or accessibility among families, particularly in rural communities.

Many families in smaller villages across Sudan rely heavily on flour and milk as staple foods, with meat largely absent from their daily diets.

“We are working to provide families of children with malnutrition with basic nutrition education as a first step towards tackling the problem. However, we face difficulties reaching villages to deliver healthcare and raise awareness,” he told Al Jazeera.

Food contamination, particularly amid unreliable electricity supplies and a lack of refrigerators in many households, makes it difficult for families to store food safely and is also a major issue.

“Families often bring their children to hospital only when malnutrition has reached an advanced stage, either because of financial hardship and fears about treatment costs or because of limited education,” he said.

articles.title: Three held after boy hurt in sword attack near Gloucester school
articles.summary: A 17-year-old boy from Gloucester has also been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.
articles.body:
Two men and a boy have been arrested after a teenager was injured in an attack involving a sword near two schools in Gloucester.

St Peter's High School and Willow Primary Academy, in Tuffley, were put into lockdown after the incident at 08:50 GMT on Friday.

Police said a 17-year-old suffered a wound "believed to have been caused by the sword".

A 19-year-old was arrested overnight on suspicion of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and affray. An 18-year-old was held on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon, assault occasioning actual bodily harm and affray. Meanwhile another 17-year-old boy was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

Listen to the latest news for Gloucestershire

The trio - who are all from Gloucester - remain in police custody for questioning.

Two men, one with a sword, had been seen chasing two boys, according to police on Friday.

Armed officers attended the scene to search for the suspects who reportedly fled on foot.

Police said the 17-year-old suffered a "superficial wound believed to have been caused by the sword".

Gloucestershire Police also said a woman who had previously been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender had been released on police bail.

At the school gates outside St Peter's High School on Friday, a pupil called Jimmy told the BBC the situation was "really scary" and that they had been told to lock doors and turn lights off.

"At the time I was scared. My heart was racing," he said.

Jimmy said pupils were locked in their classrooms for several hours.

articles.title: Americans who 'screw up' their eating should use a simple fix, says Stanford scientist
articles.summary: Christopher Gardner of Stanford says legumes like lentils, tofu and edamame are an underutilized source of protein and fiber in healthy diets.
articles.body: Living a healthy lifestyle is not as complicated as many Americans make it out to be, according to a nutrition scientist, who says people shouldn't try to be perfect but should focus on gradually improving their diet day by day. "It is simpler than people think," Christopher Gardner, Ph.D., a nutrition scientist at Stanford University and author of the book "Food Sense: What to Eat and Why," told Fox News Digital. He believes that the 80/20 rule is a solid framework for a healthy diet. The approach encourages people to make nutritious food choices about 80% of the time while allowing flexibility for indulgences the remaining 20%. NEW PROTEIN RANKING NAMES UNEXPECTED WINNER OVER BEEF, SALMON AND EGGS Gardner also works with the Stanford Prevention Research Center, where a big part of his role is trying to figure out how to get people to follow guidelines that "everybody knows" but doesn't necessarily follow, such as eating a healthier diet, exercising more and smoking less, he said. He advises against trying to follow all the latest wellness trends because, sometimes, they're not based on factual information. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER He doesn't recommend cutting out an entire food group or following a strict diet. Rather, he encourages a gradual approach. An easy way to start improving an unhealthy diet is to incorporate more vegetables, fruits and minimally processed foods. He emphasized the importance of eating legumes, adding that he feels they're an underutilized component of a healthy diet. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "Asian cultures eat a lot of tempe, tofu, edamame and soy, and Latin American cultures eat a whole bunch of bean and grain dishes, and Indian culture eats a lot of lentil dals," he said, noting that legumes are usually inexpensive and versatile. They're also a great source of protein, Gardner added, as well as fiber, which many people don't consume enough of, he pointed out. Americans also eat too much junk food, he said, adding that people often know what the healthier option is, but they still choose the "chips and candy and cake and snacks and mocha frappé frappuccino instead of black coffee." "I don't think the ultra-processed thing is like, oh, we never understood it before, and now we do. I don't really think people know that it's 200 cosmetic additives," he said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Context matters when determining the "healthier" choice, Gardner noted, using the example of coffee versus tea. Coffee and tea by themselves are unproblematic, he noted. The issue lies in the sugar, dairy and other ingredients that might be added. "I can show you volumes of studies that both are good for you," Gardner said, noting that both contain antioxidants, but the additives are what determine which is "healthier." Ultimately, different things work for different people, Gardner said, and he stays open-minded. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP What people eat is much more than just science, he acknowledged, adding that "food is comfort and food is culture and food is other things." "Whatever you screw up today, you get a do-over tomorrow and the day after," he said, so "give yourself a little grace, a little patience, a little love."

articles.title: Victims in rape cases must not feel like they are on trial, Burnham says
articles.summary: The PM was responding after a police chief said comments made during Russell Brand's trial came close to "victim blaming".
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has said the government needs to make sure that victims in rape cases do not feel like they are on trial.

His comments come after Metropolitan Police boss Sir Mark Rowley told the BBC that what he heard reported from Russell Brand's trial came very close to "victim blaming" .

The government needs to "constantly look" at how rape trials are conducted to better support alleged victims in court, the prime minister told Times Radio, although BBC News understands there are no plans to change the law around rape trials.

Actor and comedian Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault after a four-week trial in London.

During an interview with BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday, it was put to Sir Mark that Brand's defence barrister Ian Winter KC "told jurors none of the complainants had in his words 'resisted, screamed or even tried to leave'".

Sir Mark replied: "I think what I've heard reported heads towards, it's getting very close to victim blaming, which is something we've thought very hard about in policing and make sure we don't do."

He said he would support a call from the Victims' Commissioner for a legal duty that would require judges to direct juries on rape myths and misconceptions in every rape trial.

"It shouldn't be possible for inaccurate statements to be made to a jury to suggest that because a rape victim didn't behave in one way that somehow undermines their case," Sir Mark explained.

In a Times Radio interview on Saturday, Burnham said he would "look closely" at the police chief's comments.

He said the government needed to look at how to "make sure they do not leave the woman feeling like she is on trial in court".

"[I'm] always prepared to make changes," he said. "We need to encourage more women to come forward to report rape, we need to get the conviction rate up.

"All of this is part of our broader agenda as a government combatting violence against women and girls."

Pressed on whether this might lead to a change in the law, the prime minister replied: "I wouldn't rule anything out... I will study what's happened here in great detail."

Brand, who has starred in films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall, will be sentenced on Monday and is expected to face substantial jail time.

He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault after the jury deliberated for eight-and-a-half hours.

The 51-year-old was refused bail and will spend the weekend in custody.

It has since been revealed that Brand is also facing further rape allegations made by two women and has been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints. The Met said its investigation "remains ongoing".

Sir Mark told BBC Breakfast he "wouldn't be surprised if many more came forward".

In the wake of Brand's trial, Victims' Commissioner Claire Waxman said rape trials must be conducted "in a way that challenges myths and misconceptions about sexual violence".

In a social media post, Waxman wrote that "victims need confidence that the justice process is fair and based on evidence, not myths and false assumptions about rape and trauma".

Speaking to the Today programme on Saturday, director and founder of the Centre for Women's Justice Harriet Wistrich agreed that juries need to understand "underlying behaviours" without "running to judgement" over how a victim behaved in a particular way.

But former Conservative MP Anna Soubry, who has now returned to her work as a barrister where she often defends rape and sexual offence cases in the Crown court, told the BBC "people are being misled" by Sir Mark's comments.

"Every single judge in those cases must give, and does give, a very firm direction to the jury on exactly these points," she said.

As a result, she said she was " really disappointed" in the police chief and stressed "we've got to trust our juries" who are able to have an understanding of the nature of sexual offences.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line .

articles.body: Iran on Saturday said it has lifted restrictions on the range of its missiles and will demonstrate its ability to strike adversaries at unexpected locations, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Saturday, amid renewed military activity involving the United States in the Strait of Hormuz.Iran had previously restricted its missiles to a 2000-kilometre range.IRGC spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi said Tehran was prepared to respond to threats without geographical limitations and would rely on asymmetric warfare to catch its adversaries off guard."The restriction has been lifted for us. However, we must demonstrate these capabilities in practice, and we should not merely make statements beforehand. Our duty is to demonstrate our capabilities on the battlefield," Mohebbi said, according to Iran's ISNA news agency.He was speaking on the sidelines of a press conference marking the IRGC Aerospace Week in Tehran."Our warfare is asymmetric, and we can strike the enemy at a location it would never anticipate, thereby bringing it to a standstill. Rest assured that we possess such capabilities," he added.Trump claims limited strikesThe remarks came a day after US President Donald Trump said American forces had carried out fresh, limited strikes on Iran, targeting an air defence system.Describing the operation as “minor”, Trump said the US military had destroyed an Iranian anti-aircraft installation shortly after it was built.“They knocked out -- they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,” Trump told reporters after arriving in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Friday evening, according to the Associated Press (AP).Iranian state media reported hearing two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, located in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments.Responding to a question about the explosions and other incidents reported in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday night, Mohebbi said Iranian forces had carried out firing exercises, with most of the explosions resulting from air defence activity."We carried out some firing, and most of the explosions were related to air defense fire. No other incidents followed. An American aircraft was also hit during the firing," he said, according to ISNA.The IRGC spokesperson did not provide further details about the American aircraft or the circumstances in which it was hit.Trump did not disclose further details about the target of Friday's US strikes. US officials have previously assessed that most of Iran's air defence systems were destroyed or severely weakened during Israeli bombardments in June 2025 and the initial stages of the current conflict. They have also said Tehran would seek to rebuild its air defences and other military infrastructure.The US military also reported carrying out what it described as defensive strikes on Monday. articles.title: Why are oil traders refusing to buy Russian diesel after Trump-Putin deal?
articles.summary: Zero Russian diesel has reached the US as tankers divert and buyers fear legal action.
articles.body:
At least three tankers carrying Russian diesel to the United States have changed course, casting doubt over US President Donald Trump’s October deal with his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin.

Nearly a month after Trump agreed to let Russia release diesel stocks to the US and global markets, despite existing sanctions, zero diesel has reached the US, where prices have nearly doubled since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran.

Russia has sent out a total of four tankers loaded with diesel since the deal was agreed.

What’s happened to tankers carrying Russian diesel to the US?

The Russian tanker Talisman and the Sierra Leone-flagged Leruo left the Baltic port of Primorsk last month, with the US East Coast as their declared destination.

As of Thursday, however, one was heading towards Brazil and the other into the Mediterranean, according to marine analytics firm Kpler and the vessel-tracking site MarineTraffic.

A third tanker, still in the North Atlantic, has changed its destination from New York to “for orders”, leaving its unloading point open.

The Financial Times also reported that Beast, a sanctioned Seychelles-owned tanker that was loaded at the Russian port of Primorsk in late October, has set sail towards the US and is currently signalling “Atlantic”.

A deal big on numbers, but scant on details.

Trump first announced the agreement following a call with Putin on October 9. He said Russia would make more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel available immediately to US and global markets.

Long-range product tankers, which carry diesel supplies, can carry up to about 100,000 tonnes of diesel at a time.

Another 500,000 tonnes would follow in November, then 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”, Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

The agreement Trump brokered with Putin allows Russian diesel to be sold, delivered, unloaded and imported until April 7. It came after Trump blamed Ukraine for causing diesel shortages by targeting Russian energy facilities amid the Russia-Ukraine war.

It also reversed years of US policy after Washington banned imports of Russian energy following Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the US Department of the Treasury has since issued a temporary sanctions exemption, much to the ire of a cross-party group of lawmakers in the US Congress who passed a new sanctions package in the name of the late, pro-Ukraine Senator Lindsey Graham in September.

In a statement to the AP news agency, the Treasury said the exemption was “in compliance with all applicable laws”.

Russia announced its first shipment of diesel during a visit to St Petersburg in October by US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff.

Yet much about the deal remains unclear.

Neither the White House nor the Kremlin has said whether the agreement was put in writing, and neither has revealed the price to be paid for the diesel, the payment terms or which companies are involved.

How much Russian diesel is now waiting to be sold?

It’s not clear exactly, but it’s less than was promised.

The volumes involved have not been made public, but analysts say the first shipment is unlikely to deliver meaningful relief to US consumers.

US retail diesel prices topped $6 a gallon ($1.59 per litre) in September – nearly twice their pre-war levels – and have remained elevated.

“The reported shipment is equivalent to roughly two hours of US distillate consumption,” Aarathi Krishnan, CEO of Raksha Intelligence, told Al Jazeera, referring to the first tanker to be dispatched by Russia.

“Even if it arrives as planned, it will make very little difference to national supply,” he said.

Why don’t traders want to buy Russian diesel?

Despite the US Treasury temporarily authorising Russian diesel sales that would normally fall under sanctions, Congress’s ban on Russian energy imports remains in place, leaving a high level of uncertainty for traders.

New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill wrote to port and terminal operators in her state on Monday, telling them to turn away ships carrying the fuel.

She warned that “any effort to profit from the illegal trade in Russian fuel will be met with harsh penalties.”

Sherrill argued the Trump administration had no authority to override the ban.

Lawmakers have also warned banks, port authorities and fuel distributors that handling the imports could expose them to civil or criminal liability, as well as future congressional investigations.

The Trump administration claims the exemption is lawful, and no court has ruled on the dispute.

“It’s clear there’s hesitancy here in bringing these barrels onshore just because of the implications of doing so,” Matt Smith, an analyst at Kpler, told AP.

The first two diverted tankers are heading towards Brazil and the Mediterranean, according to Kpler data, and the third tanker could follow.

“Because of regulatory [and] sanctions concerns, we may not see this cargo discharge on the US Atlantic coast,” Smith told AP.

Moscow, however, insists the deal is on track.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said “all the diesel will find its buyers.”

Putin’s special envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, went further, writing on X that the reports were “fake” and “tankers destined for the US continue on course.”

articles.title: Italy’s Giorgia Meloni blames pro-Russian hackers for leak of foreign minister’s data on the dark web
articles.summary: MILAN — Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said Saturday that his personal data had been disseminated on the dark web, an encrypted part of the internet, and that he has been exposed to “threats and intimidation.”
articles.body: MILAN — Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said Saturday that his personal data had been disseminated on the dark web, an encrypted part of the internet, and that he has been exposed to “threats and intimidation.” Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for the leak. Tajani made the announcement in a social media post following a string of hoax bomb threats across Europe that caused flight diversions, security threats against broadcasters as well as recent attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems and drone incursions. “For days, cybercriminals have been spreading my personal data on the dark web and seeking other information, in fact exposing me and my family to new threats and intimidation,” Tajani said, adding that the criminals “are prepared to pay for other details on me and my loved ones.” Meloni, in a separate statement, expressed solidarity with Tajani “following the revelations about the activities of pro-Russian hackers, and the publication on the dark web of personal data.” She called attempts to sell confidential information about government officials “a matter of grave concern that must be addressed with the utmost determination.” Tajani, who is also a vice premier in Italy’s government, did not specify what kind of information had been shared, but suggested that the cyberthreat was ongoing. “I will not allow myself to be intimidated in any way,” Tajani said. “I will continue working to defend my ministry, and Italy, and I will further strengthen the ties and cooperation to protect ourselves together.” Tajani did not indicate who might be responsible for the cyberattack but reiterated the Italian government’s support for Ukraine.

articles.body: Every season we get one of those College Football Playoff rankings, and instantly everyone talks about how wrong it is. It really doesn’t matter what our opinions are. I’m sure that someone will miss out on the Playoffs and everyone will be upset about it. It is inevitable, and it seems like this year there is more parity than ever before. It feels like almost weekly we get a new top team in the nation. The current top team takes the field tonight as Miami takes on Notre Dame. Miami has passed every test to start this season, but this is arguably the biggest test of the entire year for them. They come into this game at 8-0, and they have done it behind very strong quarterback play from Darian Mensah. For the season, Mensah has thrown for 2,425 yards and 25 touchdowns with just one interception. 13 of those 25 touchdowns have gone to Malachi Toney, who is missing this game with an ankle injury. He is getting surgery on the ankle as well, so someone has to step up in a big way. I’m going to criticize Notre Dame for this, so I should probably do the same for Miami. Their schedule isn’t very impressive. Notre Dame is the only team on the schedule that is ranked, and therefore will be the first ranked team they play. They beat Stanford, Florida A&M, Wake Forest, Central Michigan, Clemson, Florida State, Pittsburgh, and North Carolina. In fairness to them, it turns out Wake Forest is good, but at the time they were not ranked. They did have a scare against Florida State, winning in a somewhat controversial way in double overtime. CFP RANKINGS: NOTRE DAME FACES SUDDEN DEATH, SEC FEELING GOOD, AND BIG TEN CLOSE TO HITTING THE PANIC BUTTON Notre Dame is one of the more frustrating schools in my opinion. They aren’t in a conference, and everyone seems to think they are a powerhouse. I haven’t been impressed by their team in most seasons. They tend to coast to wins against bad teams because they can pick whoever they want to play. This year, the Fighting Irish come into the game with a 7-1 record, having lost against BYU two games ago. That was also a controversial loss, but either way, the loss is on their record. None of these games were particularly close. They have won all of them by at least two scores. CJ Carr has put together a really strong season, but again, it is hard to assess how good he actually is considering the team has played poor competition. He has thrown 18 touchdown passes, and unlike Miami, he is spreading the ball around the field. Playing Miami, even at home, will still be a challenge, but without their best offensive weapon, it should be easier for the Fighting Irish. I do think the spread is a bit too high, though. articles.title: La federación internacional prohíbe a Bielorrusia disputar el Mundial
articles.standfirst: El TAS, sin embargo, se pronunció a favor de que Rusia sí juegue ese campeonato del mundo
articles.summary: El TAS, sin embargo, se pronunció a favor de que Rusia sí juegue ese campeonato del mundo
articles.body: La Federación Internacional de Hockey sobre Hielo (IIHF, en sus siglas en inglés) ha acordado que Bielorrusia no participe en el Mundial absoluto en mayo del próximo año, ni tampoco en el Mundial júnior que comenzará a finales de diciembre en Canadá, ambos en la categoría masculina. El Consejo de la IIHF dio a conocer este sábado en un comunicado su decisión sobre las selecciones masculinas de Bielorrusia en virtud de los principios que estableció en su congreso de 2022 tras la invasión de Ucrania por parte de Rusia con el apoyo de Bielorrusia. La decisión del órgano ejecutivo viene a cuenta del fallo de la Junta Disciplinaria de la IIHF, que confirmó parcialmente la apelación de la Asociación Bielorrusa de Hockey sobre Hielo contra las decisiones del Consejo del pasado 27 de julio de 2026. El órgano disciplinario confirmó que "no tenía fundamento legal para ordenar la reintegración inmediata". El Consejo afirma haber tenido en cuenta la organización y los acuerdos deportivos vigentes para ambos campeonatos, al igual que "las estructuras de competición, los calendarios, la venta de entradas y la planificación operativa". El Mundial absoluto masculino se celebrará en Alemania del 14 al 30 de mayo y el júnior, en Canadá del 26 de diciembre al 5 de enero. En el mismo comunicado, la IIHF vuelve a pronunciarse sobre el fallo del Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) del pasado 30 de octubre en el que da la razón a Rusia para poder participar en los diferentes Mundiales previstos en 2027 en categoría masculina y femenina. Ante la negativa de Finlandia, República Checa, Suecia, Noruega, Dinamarca y Letonia a jugar el Mundial absoluto si lo hace Rusia, la federación internacional asegura que "está explorando todas las vías disponibles". Ello incluye el inicio de conversaciones con todas las federaciones nacionales afectadas, incluida la rusa, para buscar "una solución constructiva que beneficie al hockey sobre hielo mundial". Tras reiterar su desacuerdo con el TAS, la IIHF asegura que está tomando "las medidas necesarias" que exige la resolución del órgano de arbitraje y "revisando las condiciones que deben cumplirse para salvaguardar los nuestros campeonatos, proteger la estabilidad financiera de la organización y asegurar el futuro a largo plazo del hockey sobre hielo internacional". "La IIHF debe trabajar dentro del marco aplicable, cumpliendo con su responsabilidad de preservar la competencia internacional y proteger el deporte en su conjunto", añade el organismo rector.

articles.title: '9 bullets hit victim': After killing ex-Tech Mahindra regional head Paramjeet Dhankar, neighbour tries to kill son; he escapes attack by hiding behind parked cars
articles.summary: FARIDABAD: After allegedly shooting his neighbour Paramjeet Dhankar dead, a 42-year-old former regional business head of Tech Mahindra's Asia-Pacific
articles.body: FARIDABAD: After allegedly shooting his neighbour Paramjeet Dhankar dead, a 42-year-old former regional business head of Tech Mahindra's Asia-Pacific region, a 44-year-old scrap dealer also tried to kill his son Shaurya, who escaped by taking cover behind parked cars on Friday night in Faridabad.The accused, Mohan alias Monu Sharma, was arrested from DLF Chowk in Ballabgarh on Saturday, police said.The accused allegedly opened fire at Dhankar and his son following an argument over vehicle parking in Sector 21C last night. While Dhankar sustained multiple bullet injuries and died on the spot, his son, Shaurya, managed to escape by taking cover behind parked cars.Police said the accused fired around 14-15 rounds from his licensed pistol. Nine bullets are believed to have hit Dhankar, though investigators are yet to ascertain the exact number of injuries.Parking dispute turns into deadly shootingThe shooting followed a long-running dispute between the two families over parking and a pet dog. The accused's son would allegedly make their pet dog defecate in the building's parking area, triggering repeated arguments between the neighbours.Dhankar lived with his wife, son and daughter on the first floor of house number 641, while Mohan resided on the third floor of the same building.Police said Dhankar had returned from the gym around 8pm when an argument broke out between the two men over vehicle parking. The altercation soon escalated, with Mohan allegedly pulling out his licensed pistol and opening fire.The accused also allegedly targeted Dhankar's son, Shaurya, who managed to save himself by taking cover behind parked cars.Investigators are also examining whether the earlier dispute over the pet dog contributed to the confrontation.Earlier police complaint failed to end feudThe shooting came against the backdrop of repeated disagreements between the families. Five days before the incident, Mohan had allegedly abused Dhankar's son, police said.A few days before the shooting, Dhankar's family had also approached the police with a complaint over the dispute. However, the matter was subsequently settled.The circumstances leading to Friday night's confrontation are now part of the investigation.Singapore-based executive had returned for weddingDhankar was employed with a private company in Singapore and had returned to Faridabad just two days before the shooting to attend his nephew's wedding, scheduled for November 24.He originally hailed from Hisar.According to his LinkedIn profile, he had earlier served as regional business head of Tech Mahindra's Asia-Pacific region.He was currently working as senior vice-president of FPT Software Company Limited.Stay updated with the latest Faridabad news.
